record_body:
Deal: 102884 (Enterprise Dedicated Eval) — primary risk: latency stability / tail spikes

Account summary
- Evaluating Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) for internal “LLM assistant” platform used by Support + Operations teams.
- Traffic pattern is bursty (market open / incident spikes) with a mixed distribution: some long-context doc QA + short chat turn-taking. They explicitly called out: “We can’t have random timeouts during bursts; p99 is what our business feels.”

Current state / what they’re comparing
- Currently prototyping across 2 paths: (1) hyperscaler managed endpoint, (2) self-hosted vLLM on their GPU fleet.
- Redwood appeal: performance + operational simplicity + dedicated isolation, but they need confidence that we’ve addressed allocator/fragmentation edge cases.

Key technical objections (from deep dive)
- Tail latency: saw p99 spikes in their POC load test when prefill and decode interleave under burst (their words: “it’s fine at steady-state, then it falls apart when the queue surges”).
- Memory behavior: asked specifically about KV cache fragmentation, allocator search overhead, and “holes” after sequences complete.
- OOM risk: they’re worried we’ll respond by tightening admission control (protecting the system but violating their throughput SLO).
- Observability: they want to see a clear set of signals that correlates spikes to root cause (fragmentation ratio, allocation failures, eviction rate, compaction cost) and a rollback lever if a mitigation increases median latency.

Notes from technical deep dive (Fireflies: ff-2025-02-14-technical-deep-dive-kv-cache-latency)
- Omar walked through our planned KV cache compaction improvements (block-map allocator + compaction triggers/budgets + scheduler-aware eviction).
- Customer asked if compaction implies pointer instability / kernel address changes; we clarified move semantics are controlled and guarded by stream sync points and budgets.
- They requested: written “how it works” at a level they can hand to their perf team (not marketing).
- They also asked whether compaction is on by default (answer: will be behind a runtime flag; safe staged rollout).

POC check-in (Fireflies: ff-2025-03-01-poc-checkin-latency-stability)
- They shared burst traces + mixed context lengths; biggest pain is timeouts in their internal UI.
- They said they can accept slightly higher p50 if p99/p99.9 becomes predictable.
- They want a concrete acceptance gate for the Dedicated pool: p99 < 900ms for a defined request mix at target QPS, plus “no allocator failure events” in the steady burn.

Requirements captured
- Product: Dedicated (isolation), with ability to reserve capacity and define autoscale/burst policy.
- Latency: p95 must be stable; p99 stability is the decision criterion; avoid step-function tails during burst.
- Throughput: consistent tokens/sec under spikes; avoid aggressive admission control that collapses throughput.
- Deployment: VPC preferred; security review will require SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS integration, and retention controls.
- Reliability: must have clear rollback/mitigation levers if a runtime change causes regressions.

Internal notes / mapping to current project
- This deal is directly tied to the KV cache compaction workstream (Serving Runtime Performance — Kernel + Scheduling). Their POC failures line up with known fragmentation under burst + mixed lengths.
- Recommended to share baseline + canary learnings once available (without overpromising on timelines).

Activity timeline
- 2025-02-06: Deal created from inbound enterprise eval request; Dedicated evaluation scoped.
- 2025-02-14: Technical deep dive with runtime team (ff-2025-02-14-technical-deep-dive-kv-cache-latency). Primary objection: p99 spikes under burst.
- 2025-02-20: Follow-up email thread opened to align internally on priority and messaging (thread-9d2c3f1a-kv-compaction-escalation).
- 2025-03-01: POC check-in; customer reiterates “p99 is the gate” and requests explicit metrics/alerts + rollback plan.

Next steps (2 weeks)
- Provide a short technical note: fragmentation/allocator signals, planned compaction triggers/budgets, and how scheduler participates (position as a reliability improvement, no behavior change).
- Share proposed Dedicated canary/rollback signals (what we’d alert on; what we’d flip) and confirm alignment with their perf team.
- Schedule security review kickoff; confirm data residency expectations and logging/retention boundaries.

Open questions
- Confirm exact workload mix: % long-context doc QA vs short chat; max context length they will allow; target concurrency.
- Determine if they need EU region active/active or only DR; clarify any constraints around cross-region telemetry.

Deal risk (explicit)
- If we can’t demonstrate improved tail stability (p99/p99.9) under bursty mixed-length traffic, they will default to hyperscaler managed endpoint or proceed with self-hosting despite operational cost.
